You’ll Never Guess How Much a Ferrari LaFerrari Costs These Days
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | mph
Ferrari now has a successor to the iconic LaFerrari in its portfolio. It’s called the F80, entered production last year, and only 799 units will see the light of day.
Some say it does not look that good, especially when compared to some of its iconic predecessors, but that does not mean that it’s not fast. Because it is. The 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) sprint take just 2.15 seconds, and in 5.75 seconds after taking off, it will reach 124 mph (200 kph). The top speed is 217 mph (350 kph), the spec sheet reveals.
Ferrari’s F80 weighs 3,362 lbs (1,525 kg) dry, and features a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 engine behind the passenger compartment. The ICE makes 887 hp (900 ps/662 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque at 8,750 and 5,500 rpm, respectively, and it’s backed up by a pair of electric motors mounted at the front that generated 282 hp (286 ps/210 kW).
There is also a third electric motor that drives the rear wheels, and it produces 80 hp (81 ps/60 kW). In total, this model has 1,183 hp (1,200 ps/883 kW) available via the right pedal, and that makes it superior to the LaFerrari. The latter came with 949 hp (963 ps/708 kW) in total, including 161 hp (163 ps/120 kW) produced by its electric motor (HY-KERS), and 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) and 516 lb-ft (700 Nm) of torque developed by the 6.3-liter naturally aspirated V12.
Photo: Instagram | mph Production of the Ferrari LaFerrari spanned between 2013 and 2018. The fixed-roof model was assembled between 2013 and 2016, and the open-top variant (Aperta) came to life from 2016 to 2018. Only 499 Coupes and 210 Apertas saw the light of day in total, which makes this model, which was considered a hypercar back in the day, an automotive unicorn.
However, for such a rare thing, it seems that there are always a few examples looking for new homes on the used car market worldwide. Take the one pictured in the gallery above, for instance, which lives in the United States of America, and has barely seen any action over the years. It is a 2014 model year car, according to the vendor, and at the time of cataloging, it had a mere 431 miles (694 km) under its belt.
This means that you are looking at a brand-new Ferrari LaFerrari , despite being well over a decade old, and chances are that it might retain some of that new car smell. The vendor reminds web surfers how powerful this model is, what powertrain it uses, and also mentions the Rosso Corsa exterior paint finish, which fits the model like a glove, this writer thinks. This example has red brake calipers behind the five-spoke silver alloys, and appears to be in perfect condition overall.
A few images of the interior, which accompany the ad that we will get to in a few moments, reveal the black leather upholstery, as well as plenty of red details on the seats, and red seatbelts. It seems that the pillars, headliner, and part of the steering wheel were wrapped in Alcantara, and if you must know, no, the tuning fairy hasn’t visited this example. And for what it’s worth, we (or I) believe that the cockpit has aged just fine.
Photo: Instagram | mph The same can be said about the exterior, too, because the Ferrari LaFerrari may be quite old in today’s fast-moving automotive world, but it still looks like something that could still be in production. And we can say the same thing about its two biggest rivals from back in the day, namely the Porsche 918 Spyder and the McLaren P1, which made up the so-called “Holy Trinity” of hypercars.
This Ferrari LaFerrari is definitely a collector’s item, and chances are it won’t sit long on the used car market due to the fact that it has barely been driven. Unfortunately, the vendor hasn’t said anything about the title, how many owners it has in the papers, and whether it is available for shipping nationwide, but what it did reveal was the asking price. And you may want to sit down for this one, because it is truly eye-watering.
On average, the LaFerrari Coupe fetches between $5 million and close to $9 million in today’s used car market in the United States of America, and the LaFerrari Aperta, namely the open-top variant, is a lot more expensive, as it tends to go between $7.5 and $11 million. As for the pictured example, its next owner will have to pay close to $10 million. At the time of writing, the modern-classic hypercar had a sticker price of $9,850,000 attached to it.
If you had all the money in the world, would you spend some on this barely-driven Ferrari LaFerrari? For what it’s worth, I find it a bit too pricey, but that does not make it any less cool, does it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by MPH (@mph)
